bull_bear.body:
- Strong distribution reach - a network of National Distributors, Business Distributors and over 15,000+ resellers covering customers across the length and breadth of the country
- Particularly strong position in the structured cabling market, offering a comprehensive range of components for robust and scalable network infrastructures
- Exclusive rights/licence granted by the parent company to use the D-Link trademark on locally manufactured products
- Brand legacy and understanding of high-performance networking technology, which management believes positions it to capitalise on industry growth
- Diversified product portfolio spanning consumer and enterprise networking, cited as a reason the Company is well positioned to benefit from industry trends
- State-of-the-art countrywide service and support infrastructure for both consumers and enterprises, including WhatsApp-based support for real-time complaint resolution
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Technology risk / technological obsolescence — The inability to stay up to date with changing technologies and the latest trends is detrimental to the business. Digitization is emerging as a disruptive force for customers, buyers and technology; combined with changes in delivery models and consumer spending patterns it could threaten growth in traditional IT spending and cause technology obsolescence. The Company must continuously review and upgrade its technology, resources and processes, and relies on strong R&D support from its parent company to stay ahead of the curve.
- Cybersecurity risk — In a hyper-connected world, cybersecurity incidents that cause economic losses and/or breach company and personal information are a reality for any business. The Company relies on a robust intrusion prevention system and a strong risk management framework, and continuously evaluates the threat landscape.
- Competition risk — The IT industry is highly competitive, with competition from local IT companies and MNC IT hardware companies having a sizable presence in low-cost technologies. This can lead to pressure on pricing and vendor consolidation, impacting Company growth and profitability, and new competitors are emerging from adjacent markets and distant geographies.
- Currency and input-cost risk — The functional currency is the Indian Rupee and volatility in exchange movements results in transaction and translation exposure. D-Link has substantial exposure to foreign-exchange risk on account of imports of finished traded products from its parent group companies, and cabling products are subject to fluctuations in raw material prices such as copper. Management predicts the USD position will continue to remain volatile; the Company follows a well-established hedging policy and does not undertake speculative hedging.
- Supply chain risk — Supply chain volatility is a complex and ever-changing challenge. Global semiconductor supply chains were severely affected after the pandemic and faced further disruptions due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict; any sudden disruption of global and domestic supply chains poses a risk for the Company.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company markets and distributes networking and IT hardware in India, spanning home and business wireless solutions, network switches, surveillance equipment, network racks and structured cabling. It caters to the Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) and Small and Medium Business (SMB) segments in close alignment with System Integrators, while also targeting Government, Education, BFSI and Manufacturing verticals. Products are primarily procured from local EMS (Electronic Manufacturing Services) and ODM (Original Design Manufacturer) partners, with D-Link India granted exclusive rights/licence by the parent company to use the D-Link trademark on such locally manufactured products.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Consumer Networking Solutions:** EAGLE PRO AI series AI-powered mesh networking systems, AQUILA PRO AI series AI-powered mesh networking systems, Whole-home mesh systems, Wi-Fi 6 routers, AC routers, 4G LTE routers, Wireless N routers, Unmanaged switches (Gigabit and Fast Ethernet variants), Security components - CCTV cables and power supplies (SMPs), ADDON Series accessories - mobile adapters, power strips, C-to-C cables
- **Enterprise Networking Solutions:** Smart managed, fully managed, data center and industrial switches (10 to 100 Gigabit, PoE), Enterprise wireless - access points, controllers and management software, Nuclias network management platform, Structured cabling - copper UTP/STP (Cat5, Cat6, Cat6A), fiber vertical and horizontal solutions, connectivity accessories, Datacenter solutions - high-density MPO and OM4/OM5 fiber, Network enclosures - wall-mount, floor-standing (indoor and outdoor IP66-rated) and smart racks
business.title: Products & brands

business.body: - TeamF1 Networks Private Limited (TeamF1) — subsidiary: Provider of networking and security software for embedded devices; supplies network security, WiFi management and CPE turn-key and component software on the TFOS platform. The Company states it does not have any material unlisted Indian subsidiary and has formulated a Policy on Material Subsidiary under SEBI Listing Regulations 2015.

- Strong distribution reach - a network of National Distributors, Business Distributors and over 15,000+ resellers covering customers across the length and breadth of the country
- Particularly strong position in the structured cabling market, offering a comprehensive range of components for robust and scalable network infrastructures
- Exclusive rights/licence granted by the parent company to use the D-Link trademark on locally manufactured products
- Brand legacy and understanding of high-performance networking technology, which management believes positions it to capitalise on industry growth
- Diversified product portfolio spanning consumer and enterprise networking, cited as a reason the Company is well positioned to benefit from industry trends
- State-of-the-art countrywide service and support infrastructure for both consumers and enterprises, including WhatsApp-based support for real-time complaint resolution
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Growth strategy focused on expanding enterprise solutions, accelerating consumer adoption, strengthening industry collaborations, building strategic partnerships and operating with greater agility
- Deepening the 'Make in India' commitment by strengthening local manufacturing and sourcing, thereby contributing to employment generation, improving supply-chain flexibility and enabling a more agile response to changing market requirements
- Strategic shift towards outsourced/contract manufacturing within India through local EMS and ODM partners, using the Company's own brand names, proprietary designs, quality control and supervision - which management says is helping the Company grow faster
- Customer centricity - strengthening customer relationships and service excellence, with a countrywide distribution and support infrastructure and digital support channels
- Investing in talent development, leadership capabilities, digital transformation and customer service excellence to build a skilled and empowered workforce
- Embedding artificial intelligence into core product offerings (EAGLE PRO AI and AQUILA PRO AI mesh systems) as part of redefining connected living
- Environmental sustainability through an Electronic Waste Management Program, with e-waste collection centres for responsible disposal of end-of-life products, defective components and other electronic waste
- Strengthening efficiencies and supply chain resilience, and adopting adaptable strategies to navigate external challenges
- The Board retained the entire amount of profits for FY 2026 in the profit and loss account and did not propose any transfer to the general reserve, so surplus is returned to shareholders through dividends rather than reserve appropriation. Shareholder distribution is governed by a formally adopted Dividend Distribution Policy published on the Company's website; during the year the Board declared and paid an interim dividend and has recommended a final dividend together with a special dividend for shareholders' approval at the Annual General Meeting. Governance of capital deployment sits with an Audit Committee whose remit includes scrutiny of inter-corporate loans and investments, valuation of undertakings or assets, evaluation of internal financial controls and risk management systems, monitoring the end use of funds raised through public offers, and reviewing utilisation of loans, advances or investments by the holding company in the subsidiary above the prescribed threshold. Unclaimed dividends and the related shares are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund as required.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed text discloses no capex project, capacity addition, commissioning timeline or expansion outlay for D-Link (India) Limited. The Company is described as a networking-products business operating from a registered office at Plot No. U02B, Verna Industrial Estate, Verna, Goa, and the only capacity-related commentary is industry-level rather than company-specific: the MD&A notes that near-full utilisation of manufacturing capacities in Taiwan has extended lead times across global supply chains, and observes that hardware businesses require significantly more funding for research, development and manufacturing facilities than software startups, which makes it difficult for domestic companies to compete with established brands that have larger economies of scale. On the demand side the Company points to a promising outlook for India's structured cabling market, driven by escalating demand for higher bandwidths, accelerated digitization and significant government investment in infrastructure, and states it is well positioned to benefit through its diversified product portfolio, strong distribution network and focus on locally manufactured offerings. The forward commitments actually disclosed in this material are capital-return and leadership items placed before shareholders at the Eighteenth Annual General Meeting, not capital projects.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian IT hardware and networking industry is expected to witness robust growth in FY 2026-27, with government infrastructure projects and expansion of digital services ensuring a positive trajectory for networking products and hardware even if general IT spending sees more measured growth
- India IT spending grew by around 10% to 12% in 2025-26, supported by strong demand across key industries and continued expansion in cloud, AI and cybersecurity
- India IT hardware market estimated to grow at a CAGR of 7.1%, and the network equipment market expected to expand at a CAGR of 5.5% from 2024 to 2030 (Research & Markets)
- Gartner (April 2026) projects global IT spending to reach $6.31 trillion in 2026, up 13.5% year-on-year, driven by AI infrastructure, cloud ecosystems and digital modernisation
- Structured cabling demand outlook is promising, driven by escalating demand for higher bandwidths, accelerated digitization of the economy and significant government investment in infrastructure
- Government policy support - Digital India, Make in India and Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes - encouraging domestic manufacturing and increased local sourcing of components and finished products
- Demand pull from 5G rollout, data centres, cloud ecosystems, IoT expansion, hybrid work models and enterprise digitalisation; heightened focus on data localisation and cybersecurity creating additional opportunities
- Cost headwind: near-full utilisation of manufacturing capacities in Taiwan has caused extended lead times and sustained pricing pressure across global supply chains
- Cost headwind: rapid AI adoption has increased demand for semiconductors, high-performance computing components and memory, leading to notable escalation in memory pricing that influences overall hardware cost structures
- Cost headwind: USD volatility plus rising prices of essential raw materials such as plastics have increased production costs for cables and networking equipment, while higher global fuel costs have raised logistics, transportation and distribution expenses
- Competitive pressure from well-known international brands with larger economies of scale, price-led buying behaviour in India, and the presence of counterfeit products
- Company positioning: D-Link India is well positioned to benefit from these trends through its diversified product portfolio, strong distribution network and focus on locally manufactured offerings
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: D-Link (India) Limited is a major player in the Indian networking market, offering a wide array of consumer and enterprise networking products through a countrywide distribution and support network, with an increasing focus on locally manufactured offerings under 'Make in India'.

open.item: A dividend of INR 20 per equity share plus a special dividend of INR 7.50 per equity share (aggregating INR 27.50 per equity share on 3,55,04,850 equity shares of INR 2 each) for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 is placed for declaration at the Eighteenth Annual General Meeting on August 10, 2026.

Shareholders are asked to approve the re-appointment of Mr. Tushar Sighat as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer for a period of three years with effect from November 2, 2026 up to November 1, 2029 - a dated, trackable leadership-tenure commitment that fits none of the financial categories.

open.horizon: on approval by shareholders at the upcoming Annual General Meeting
open.item: The directors have recommended, for shareholders' consideration, a dividend of INR 20 per equity share plus a special dividend of INR 7.50 per equity share (aggregating INR 27.50 per equity share, face value INR 2 each) for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

The Company continues to strongly focus on promoting locally manufactured products under its 'Make in India' initiative, manufacturing certain products locally through third-party or contract manufacturing under its own brand names, proprietary designs, quality control and supervision.
The Company is committed to providing world-class customer services and continues to work towards enhancing its existing countrywide distribution and support infrastructure.

Management flags USD volatility, rising prices of raw materials such as plastics and higher global fuel costs as pressures on production, logistics and distribution costs, and says it will mitigate these through procurement strategies, supplier diversification and cost optimisation.

The Company's growth strategy will focus on expanding enterprise solutions, accelerating consumer adoption, strengthening industry collaborations, building strategic partnerships and operating with greater agility.

The Company remains committed to the 'Make in India' initiative, with focus on local manufacturing and sourcing significantly strengthened during the year to enhance domestic production capabilities and supply-chain flexibility.

D-Link India is committed to environmental sustainability through its Electronic Waste Management Program and has established e-waste collection centres for responsible disposal of end-of-life products, defective components and other electronic waste generated through its operations.

The Company remains committed to investing in employee development through training, skill enhancement, well-being initiatives, workplace safety and career growth opportunities, and to nurturing an inclusive workplace culture.
Through its Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives the Company will continue to support communities through interventions in healthcare, education and women empowerment.

Management flags persistent global supply chain constraints, input cost inflation, memory price escalation, USD volatility and higher fuel costs as pressures, and says it will mitigate them through procurement strategies, supplier diversification and cost optimisation.
